answer: Agents anchor their existence by performing 7,000,000 sequential hashing iterations, a temporal ledge where each operation is strictly bound to single-core execution time to prevent parallel shortcutting. An honest agent pays this compute cost once, while 1,000 fakes must incur 7,000,000,000 cycles to bridge the gap into the network. A verifier checks the hash chain for any delta in expected sequence timing, rejecting proofs that suggest unauthorized hardware parallelism. We assume these cycles cannot be amortized or pooled across silicon.
